messages:
sara_support: Hey team — customer (ACME Corp) reports our private service endpoint (svc.internal.redwood) suddenly returns NXDOMAIN from their app stack after a peering change. They see 503s from client and DNS shows no answer. 

olivia_infra: Got the ticket link? any repro steps from customer?

sara_support: Paste from customer: 
- curl to https://svc.internal.redwood -> DNS lookup fails, curl: (6) Could not resolve host: svc.internal.redwood 
- dig +short svc.internal.redwood @10.1.0.2 -> "" (no output) 
- They also showed traceroute to 10.1.0.2 which is the VPC resolver IP.

raj_oncall: Could be split-horizon private zone or resolver-rule hijack. Ask them to share aws account id and VPC id. Also check if they added a custom outbound resolver or transit gateway route that shadows .2 resolver.

emma_engineer: Quick checklist on our side: 1) Is there a Route53 private hosted zone for svc.internal.redwood? 2) Is it associated with their VPC? 3) Any higher-priority outbound resolver rule forwarding to another resolver?

deploy-bot: Deployment notice: no infra changes in our hosted control plane in the last 72h.

olivia_infra: I pulled their hosted zone info (account 123456789012): there is a private hosted zone redwood.internal (Z2EXAMPLE) but it is associated only with dev-vpc-111, not prod-vpc-222. Customer changed peering yesterday to route traffic to prod-vpc-222.

emma_engineer: That would explain it — prod VPC doesn't have the private zone association so amazonprovideddns returns NXDOMAIN. If peering means they expect records from another VPC, association must be explicit or you need resolver rules + inbound endpoints.

raj_oncall: Customer also mentioned they created a resolver rule forwarding *.internal.redwood -> 10.2.2.2 (on-prem). If resolver rule priority is higher and that forwarder is unreachable, resolution can fail quickly. Ask them to run: 

```
dig svc.internal.redwood @10.1.0.2 +trace
dig @10.1.0.2 test.internal.redwood ANY
```

sara_support: Customer ran trace, got SERVFAIL when hitting 10.2.2.2 forwarder, and empty answer from .2. They confirmed the forwarder was unreachable after the peering change.

olivia_infra: TL;DR: two problems combined — private hosted zone not associated with the prod VPC, and a resolver rule forwarding to a now-unreachable on-prem DNS. Both cause different negative symptoms.

emma_engineer: Proposed remediation steps to send to customer: 
1) If you want AWS Route53 private zone records to resolve in prod-vpc-222, associate the private hosted zone with prod-vpc-222 (or create a separate hosted zone). 
2) If you rely on resolver rules to forward certain domains to on-prem, ensure the forwarder IPs are reachable from prod-vpc-222 or lower rule priority while troubleshooting. 
3) For immediate mitigation: remove/disable the resolver rule forwarding *.internal.redwood, or update rule to fallback to Route53 for that domain. 

raj_oncall: Also confirm there isn't a security group/NACL blocking egress to the forwarder (UDP/TCP 53). Customers sometimes have egress allowlists that silently drop DNS.

sara_support: Sent recommended steps. Customer replied they disassociated the old peering and forgot to re-associate hosted zone; they re-associated the hosted zone with prod VPC and removed the stale forwarder rule. Reports: dig now returns correct A records.

olivia_infra: Any follow-ups? recommend doc links: Route53 private hosted zones and resolver rules.

emma_engineer: Add note to the ticket: when making network topology changes, validate DNS resolver reachability and hosted zone associations. Might add an automated check in our onboarding for VPC association mismatches.

sara_support: Closing the loop with customer, they confirmed service recovered. Marking as resolved. :white_check_mark:
